ai.description: This robust frog reaches 6–8 cm. It features a mottled brown or olive back with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and a white belly. Key traits include a pointed snout and powerful, webbed hind limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphaerotheca dobsonii* is best distinguished by its distinct, shovel-shaped inner metatarsal tubercle, which is significantly larger and more prominent than in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Mangalore Bullfrog inhabits lowland areas, typically found in moist deciduous forests, agricultural fields, and near temporary water bodies at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Mangalore bullfrog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes a sit-and-wait foraging strategy, remaining motionless to ambush passing insects and small vertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphaerotheca dobsonii* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 500–1,000 eggs in temporary rain pools. It is an explosive breeder with an aquatic larval stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sphaerotheca dobsonii* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Maharashtra across low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Mangalore Bullfrog produces a low-pitched, resonant "gurr" or "tok" sound, typically heard as single, explosive calls from temporary monsoon pools and ditches.
